subject: Request: availability exemption for Nimbus-v2 preview pilot
messages:
From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@cobalthealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Cobalt Health Security <security@cobalthealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: availability exemption for Nimbus-v2 preview pilot

Hi Markus / Laura,

We are preparing a 6-week pilot with our clinical triage team to validate Redwood's Nimbus-v2 (preview) for structured note generation. The pilot window we have in mind is Sep 28 -> Nov 9. Because Nimbus-v2 is a preview model, our security and procurement teams require a written exception to Redwood's standard uptime and latency SLAs for the duration of the pilot.

Specifically we need:
- a documented temporary change to the uptime SLO (we can accept a lower monthly uptime for the pilot)
- a latency guidance for p95 calls (our UX team wants to set expectations)
- an operator contact and rollback procedure in case of production impact

Attached is a short pilot plan and the security questionnaire items that triggered this. Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a short-term waiver and what guardrails you will apply (fallback model, rate caps, monitoring hooks, compensation terms if severe outages)? We also need a signed waiver (DocuSign) to present to our legal/compliance team.

Thanks — Tom
Tom Reynolds
Head of Clinical Product, Cobalt Health
[Attachment: pilot-metrics-template.csv]
[Attachment: pilot-plan.pdf]

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-20T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: availability exemption for Nimbus-v2 preview pilot

Team — quick triage. Tom from Cobalt asking for a written exception for Nimbus-v2 preview during a 6-week pilot. Key asks: temporary uptime SLA change, latency guidance, operator contact, and DocuSign waiver.

My initial thoughts: we can grant a timeboxed exception if we require:
- a rollback/fallback to Nimbus-v1 automatically on error rates or elevated latency (configurable by route)
- a cap on overall QPS for the pilot to protect multi-tenant capacity
- daily health-check reports and a single point of contact for incident escalation

Laura — can you confirm whether Legal can approve a 6-week SLO carveout with the waiver language?
Dev — can Platform Ops provide a fallback config and a canary window; how fast can we create an automated fallback that preserves request headers for audit?
Rishi — please outline what monitoring we should require in the runbook (metrics, alert thresholds).

I want to move fast on this; Cobalt is close to committing to Dedicated if pilot looks good.

-MK
Markus Klein
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@cobalthealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-21T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: availability exemption for Nimbus-v2 preview pilot

Tom — thanks for the clear note and the attachments. We appreciate Cobalt's thoughtful approach.

Redwood can provide a conditional, timeboxed availability exemption for the Nimbus-v2 preview pilot with the following terms:

1) Duration and scope
- Pilot window: 2026-09-28 to 2026-11-09 (6 weeks).
- Applies only to the production routes agreed in the attached pilot-plan.

2) Adjusted commitments (pilot-only)
- Monthly uptime objective: 99.0% for the pilot month(s) covering the window (instead of our standard 99.9%).
- Latency guideline: p95 <= 300ms. We will publish real-time p95 on the pilot dashboard; this is a target not a contractual credit trigger for the pilot.

3) Guardrails and mitigations
- Automatic fallback to Nimbus-v1 on sustained error-rate > 1.5% for 5m or p95 latency > 1s for 3m. Fallback behavior will add an "x-redwood-fallback: nimbus-v1" header.
- Rate limiting: pilot QPS will be capped to the agreed test profile in pilot-metrics-template.csv to protect other tenants.
- Daily health digest (automated) to Cobalt's security distribution and the technical contact.

4) Approvals and paperwork
- Redwood will provide a short waiver (DocuSign) that documents the temporary availability exemption and required runbook controls.
- Cobalt must sign the waiver before the pilot start date.

5) Escalation and rollback
- Primary escalation: platform-oncall@redwood.ai (24/7) and Markus Klein as account lead.
- Immediate rollback: Dev Patel and oncall will trigger regional rollback and notify the pilot distribution list; rollback timeline is expected <30 minutes for the route if automatic fallback is insufficient.

I have attached the waiver draft and a runbook template (nimbus-v2-preview-runbook.md). If these terms look acceptable we will issue the DocuSign link and create an internal support ticket to track the canary steps.

Best,
Laura Bennett
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: slo-waiver-form.pdf]
[Attachment: nimbus-v2-preview-runbook.md]

From: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@cobalthealth.com>

Subject: Re: Request: availability exemption for Nimbus-v2 preview pilot

Laura / Markus — this looks good and aligns with what our legal and security teams asked for. Two quick clarifications before we sign:

1) Can you confirm that the daily health digest will include raw p95/p99, error-rate, and the fallback counts? Security wants the data retained for 90 days.
2) Please confirm the named on-call contact for weekends (we need a phone number or pager).

If you can confirm those two items we will sign the waiver and execute the DocuSign. Also please include the rollback playbook in the runbook (we may add a brief audit requirement).

Thanks — Tom
